title: Structured Streaming in Spark: The Basics

scenes.line1: How does Spark handle real-time data?
scenes.say: How does Apache Spark process real-time data streams? Let's break down Structured Streaming.

scenes.label: Streams
scenes.sub: Spark treats streams as unbounded tables.
scenes.say: Structured Streaming treats incoming data as an unbounded table, not a static dataset.

rows.b: Write streaming jobs like batch code
Process data by actual event time
Results update as new data arrives

scenes.say: You use the familiar DataFrame API. Structured Streaming supports event-time processing, stateful operations, and keeps your results up to date as new data arrives.

scenes.title: Read from Kafka
scenes.say: For example, you can read from Kafka and write to a sink using readStream and writeStream.
Watermarking helps with late data, while checkpointing lets Spark recover from failures. But exactly-once processing also depends on your data sources and sinks.

scenes.question: Do watermarking and checkpointing guarantee exactly-once?
scenes.right: No. They help, but exactly-once depends on your sink and source.
scenes.say: Watch out: watermarking and checkpointing help, but they don't guarantee exactly-once. That depends on your source and sink.
